summary:
Base Artemis is an interactive, browser-based STEM mission simulator designed for young explorers. Players command a lunar outpost across a realistic 28-day lunar cycle: 14 days of scorching sunlight and solar flares followed by 14 days of freezing lunar night with zero solar power.
To survive, balance competing systems using power ratios grounded in open NASA studies: Thermal Control (TCS), Water and Oxygen recycling (ECLSS), Space Agriculture (Greenhouse), and Radiation Protection (Storm Shelter). Instead of oversimplified clicker mechanics or overwhelming engineering spreadsheets, the simulator features a reactive spacecraft cockpit, live resource bars, and clear mission alerts. When a mission fails due to blackout, starvation, radiation, or oxygen loss, the game provides an educational engineering debrief explaining why it happened and how to improve.
This project is important because it turns abstract STEM concepts into hands-on critical thinking—helping young astronauts intuitively experience the real engineering trade-offs behind NASA’s Artemis missions.
details:
Overview & Purpose

Base Artemis: Lunar Mission Simulator is a turn-based educational STEM game built to make real spaceflight engineering trade-offs visual, intuitive, and engaging for young explorers. Rather than hiding physics behind complex spreadsheets or oversimplifying survival into a basic clicker, the simulator challenges students to keep a 4-person lunar crew alive through one complete 28-day lunar cycle.

How the Simulation Works

1. Extreme 14-Day / 14-Night Cycle:

- Days 1–14 (Lunar Day): Solar panels generate +18 kW per day. Players must power cooling, life support, and salad racks while charging the base's Energy Reserve (Li-ion Batteries + Regenerative Fuel Cells) up to 100 kW-days.

- Days 15–28 (Lunar Night): The Sun sets below the horizon and solar output drops to 0 kW for 14 consecutive days. Players must switch systems into economy modes, shut down power-heavy agriculture, and carefully ration stored energy, water/oxygen, and food until sunrise.

2. Competing Subsystems & Engineering Trade-Offs:

Each turn, players balance 3 interacting modules using ratios scaled from real NASA engineering data (1 game unit = 1 kW):

- Thermal Control (TCS): Normal (2 kW day / 5 kW night), Night Economy (3 kW night by folding radiators, causing -2 Crew Health from cold), Storm Shelter (4 kW radiation protection), or OFF (0 kW, -15 Health).

- Water & Oxygen (ECLSS): Full Closed-Loop recycling (3 kW, 0% tank loss), Night Economy (1 kW, breathes from reserves at -3% per day), or OFF (0 kW, -20% per day).

- Greenhouse: OFF (0 kW, -4 food/day), Veggie Salad (3 kW, cuts food consumption to -2/day and grants +1 Health from fresh vitamins), or Full Board (60 kW for +2 food/day—an intentional NASA engineering lesson demonstrating why 100% space farming triggers an immediate Blackout, requiring freeze-dried food supplies instead).

3. Solar Flares & Educational Feedback:

- On Days 6 and 12, NASA Solar Alerts warn players of incoming Solar Flares. Failing to switch TCS to Storm Shelter (4 kW) inflicts -15 radiation damage to the crew.

- Visual Cockpit UI: An interactive spacecraft viewport dynamically changes from golden Lunar Day to red Solar Storm alerts and starry Lunar Night, paired with live resource progress bars.

- Failure Debriefs: If the mission fails due to Blackout, Starvation, Radiation, or O2 depletion, the simulator explains the exact engineering cause and gives an actionable tip for the next attempt.

Tools & Technologies Used

- Frontend & Game Logic: Pure HTML5, CSS3 (Flexbox, Grid, custom SVG lunar horizon, and dynamic CSS transitions), and Vanilla JavaScript—built as a single lightweight file with zero external dependencies so it runs smoothly in any browser or mobile device.

- Hosting & Source Control: GitHub and GitHub Pages.

- Live Playable Simulator: https://tarantaika-pixel.github.io/base-artemis-simulator/

- Open-Source Repository: https://github.com/tarantaika-pixel/base-artemis-simulator
